In another case, BaFin prohibited a public offering without a prospectus: The provider had issued "tokenized bearer bonds" according to their own statement. In doing so, they had not taken into account that security tokens are subject to prospectus requirements under certain conditions. They had contacted numerous small investors and offered them an investment opportunity in hotel properties at sought-after locations. The bearer bonds were to be tokenized, meaning digitally represented on a blockchain. The prohibition by BaFin is final and conclusive.

BaFin does not tolerate circumvention of the prospectus requirement
In 2024, BaFin focused particularly on providers of investment assets who relied on a statutory exemption from the prospectus requirement. It increasingly took action against public offers where providers had unjustifiably claimed the prospectus exemption, which according to § 2 paragraph 1 no. 3a) of the German Investment Products Act (Vermögensanlagengesetz) applies to offers of no more than 20 shares. BaFin has – among other things in its workshop on investment assets – made it clear that exemptions are to be interpreted narrowly and that it will take decisive action against providers who circumvent the prospectus requirement through abusive interpretation of the exemptions.

Objection procedures
BaFin can issue administrative acts that impose burdens, such as capital surcharges, the appointment of special representatives, winding-up orders, or prohibitions. Against these, the addressees can file an objection with BaFin (see Table 16) – within one month from the notification of the administrative act.

Summary and legal proceedings
An objection and an action for annulment against a burdensome administrative act generally have a suspensive effect (§ 80 paragraph 1 of the Administrative Court Order (Verwaltungsgerichtsordnung, VwGO)). In such cases, BaFin cannot enforce the administrative act and may not take enforcement measures.

However, there are exceptions: The suspensive effect of the administrative act may be excluded by law or due to a special order by BaFin. Then the administrative act must also be complied with if an objection has been filed. Thus, measures that BaFin takes, for example, against operators of unauthorized businesses are immediately enforceable by law. Addressees of such measures can only apply for an interim order from the administrative court to restore the suspensive effect of their legal remedy. 4 Communication
VII
Press Work and Social Media In organizing their events, BaFin applies the
In press work and through social media channels, the guideline for the sustainable organization of events. This is part of the government's "Sustainability" program of measures
the first-time appointment of a Consumer Protection Commissioner was intensively accompanied. The same applies to the start of Julia Wiens, who has been leading BaFin's insurance and pension supervision as Executive Director since January 2024. The focus was also on measures against unauthorized financial activities by Reichsbürger (Reich citizens) and against crypto fraudsters. Another focus was the media coverage of supervisory actions in insolvencies and distress situations, such as in the real estate sector, and BaFin's intervention in cases of inadequate precautions against money laundering and terrorist financing.

The media work also focused on measures with which BaFin ensured the proper business organization of regional banks. To make BaFin even more present in collective consumer protection and to promote the financial knowledge of consumers, BaFin expanded its activities to Instagram.

In 2024, BaFin published around 400 postings on its social media channels and 17 press releases. It also held two major press conferences.

Events In 2024, BaFin conducted eleven external events, in presence and digital formats. The main goal was to inform supervised entities about current or future supervisory topics. The events also served as an exchange with companies in the financial sector as well as with other authorities and institutions from Germany and abroad.

New in 2024 was the digital information series on the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) and the first-ever Forum on Audit Control and Corporate Reporting. In September, BaFin invited to a conference on the occasion of the ten-year existence of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM). Furthermore, BaFin organized established formats such as the annual insurance supervision conference, the Economic Crime Practice Forum, the IT Supervision Conference, and the specialist conference on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, in addition to the press events mentioned above.

Website and Speeches In 54 speeches and at 23 panel discussions, the President and other members of the BaFin Directorate addressed important developments around BaFin and the financial sector in 2024. Selected speeches are available on BaFin's website.

In 2024, BaFin also published 44 specialist articles, opinion pieces, and interviews on its website. In addition, it informed on its website in numerous reports about unauthorized business, BaFin's measures and sanctions, and consumer protection topics. A focus in 2024 was the numerous articles and interviews about DORA. The communication about DORA on BaFin's website was part of a larger information campaign and was closely linked with numerous posts on BaFin's social media channels and the digital information series described above.

A central publication of BaFin in 2024 was again "Risks in Focus". In it, BaFin addresses the risks that can most endanger the stability and integrity of the financial markets in Germany. It also describes what it does to contain these risks. In its annual report published in 2024, BaFin provides an overview of its work in the previous year.

Together with the Federal Working Group for Seniors (BAGSO), BaFin published three issues of the compact information series Finanzen.Information.Tipps. The goal: to inform older people about various financial topics in a way that meets their needs.

"Foreign Banks Since January 1, 2024, every financing-
II
The operation of banking transactions and the provision of financial services are subject to licensing requirements – also for institutions based in Germany whose shareholders are located outside of Germany. In 2024, the BaFin granted a license for the first time to an Asian development bank: the Korea Development Bank, a state-owned development bank based in Seoul, Republic of Korea.

The propriety of the business organization was also a focus of the supervision of foreign institutions in 2024. The differences between the supervisory regimes of countries outside Europe and the German or European requirements often pose challenges for the institutions.

1.2.3 Development of Payment and E-Money Institutions

The number of new applications for a license under the ZAG remained at a high level in 2024. In 2024, the BaFin issued nine licenses and one registration under the ZAG. Thus, at the end of 2024, a total of 83 institutions had a license or registration to provide payment services or to operate e-money business.12

In ongoing supervision, the BaFin continued to focus primarily on compliance with the requirements for proper business organization at these institutions. At two institutions, it intensified supervision by ordering special audits. Another focus of the audit was information technology.

1.2.4 Development of Financing Leasing and Factoring Institutions

In 2024, the number of supervised financing leasing and factoring institutions decreased to 366 (previous year: 385).13

The BaFin conducted four special audits at these institutions in accordance with § 44 paragraph 1 KWG. In addition to the usual interval audits, there were also event-driven special audits, in which the financial supervisory authority sometimes used forensic investigation methods.

1.2.5 Development of Crypto Custody Business and Crypto Securities Registry Management

In 2024, six additional companies received a license under § 32 paragraph 1 KWG for the crypto custody business, including a credit institution that falls under the European Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR). One institution returned the license in 2024. Thus, 14 institutions had a license to provide the financial service of crypto custody at the end of 2024.

The number of ongoing procedures for applications from companies without a full banking license for a crypto custody license has been reduced to two. Four applicants withdrew their applications, and the BaFin also denied one license. In addition, the BaFin issued the first three licenses for crypto securities registry management.

1.2.6 Credit Servicing Institutions under the Credit Secondary Market Act

The provision of credit servicing is subject to licensing requirements since December 30, 2023. This is due to the implementation of Directive (EU) 2021/2167 on credit servicers and credit purchasers through the KrZwMG. The law also regulates the obligations of buyers and sellers of claims from distressed credit contracts and the supervision of companies that provide credit services.

In 2024, the BaFin granted 26 companies the license to provide credit services under the KrZwMG. The BaFin provided market participants with extensive information on its website about the licensing procedure and the notification and reporting obligations they must comply with after being granted a license.

Convictions in major market manipulation case
In May 2024, ALMA was supplemented with a Machine Learning (ML) algorithm that supports the detection of market abuse. The ML algorithm was trained on over 1,500 datasets of real, suspicious trading patterns that BaFin has investigated over the past five years. The algorithms used for ALMA are continuously evaluated and further developed.

The process was based primarily on nine criminal complaints from BaFin from the years 2018 to 2021. The Mannheim public prosecutor's office had summarized these into a large market manipulation investigation complex and charged the suspects at the Mannheim Regional Court.

In 2024, BaFin identified indications of market manipulation in 18 analyses. In such analyses and the resulting investigations, BaFin proceeds in a risk-oriented manner: It focuses on the most relevant violations - for example, those with the potentially largest volume and/or particularly serious possible violations.

In addition, there were numerous complaints about problems with the accessibility of customer service and the long processing time of customer inquiries. The BaFin also received around 200 complaints about closed public alternative investment funds (AIFs), which are managed by the same investment management company.

As in 2023, numerous investors also complained about the incorrect transmission of tax cost basis values and the transfer of US depositary receipts.

Consumer Telephone
In 2024, 33,650 calls were received at the consumer telephone service (previous year: 28,261). Of these, 15.79 percent were related to the insurance sector, 56.77 percent to the banking sector, and 7.53 percent to the securities sector.

Investment and Asset Management Companies
In 2024, BaFin received 105 complaints and 61 inquiries regarding investment and asset management companies (previous year: 182 complaints and 42 inquiries). The focus was on issues such as distribution authorizations and the settlement and liquidation of open real estate special assets. In addition, BaFin received a total of eight inquiries and complaints about Riester pension contracts.
